title: Recovery windows rather than immediate clean-access assumptions

definition.title: Recovery windows rather than immediate clean-access assumptions
definition.source_excerpt: Encoded six seconds of H.264 with periodic intra refresh, no B frames and one reference frame. Parsed recovery-point SEI directly. Cuts at source packet indices 30, 60, 90 and 120 each advertise recovery_frame_cnt=18 and exact_match_flag=1 [S7]. For each cut, a fresh decoder receives source parameter sets plus the remaining compressed packets. showall is used to expose imperfect warm-up frames instead of hiding them. Frame hashes are compared with uninterrupted decoding of the same source. All four cuts have incorrect warm-up frames and first reach a permanently identical suffix at offset 18 frames. The tested conservative admission rule suppresses through the signaled count, admitting at offset 19. Every admitted suffix is exact. At 30 frames/s, the observed first exact suffix starts 0.6 seconds after the cut; this is a fixture-specific media recovery interval, not a startup-time benchmark.
definition.impact_basis: Potentially removes substantial work from an eligible playback, seek, preparation, retention or repeated interaction. Scope comes from the cited card; exposure and effect size are unmeasured.

definition.shared_prerequisite: Existing preview or decoder access path. Its absence is setup cost, not permission to create a complete preview service.
